title: Self-powered organic photodiodes and phototransistors for circuits and bioelectronics
abstract: Photodiodes et phototransistors organiques auto-alimentés pour les circuits et la bioélectronique Cette thèse développe des photodétecteurs à base de semi-conducteurs organiques fonctionnant sans alimentation externe et propose une plateforme intégrée pour leur application aux circuits et aux dispositifs bioélectroniques. En couvrant l'ensemble de la chaîne de la récolte d'énergie, des photodiodes auto-alimentées et des phototransistors organiques jusqu'à l'implémentation de circuits et aux applications de biosignaux elle établit la faisabilité de systèmes optoélectroniques auto-alimentés ainsi que les technologies fondamentales nécessaires à leur déploiement pratique. Des nanogénérateurs triboélectriques (TENG) et des cellules photovoltaïques organiques (PV) ont été conçus comme sources d'énergie embarquées pour les photodétecteurs, avec une évaluation systématique des caractéristiques de sortie, de la densité de puissance et de la stabilité. Des photodiodes organiques auto-alimentées (OPD) ont ensuite été réalisées et analysées en faible éclairement en termes de réponse photoélectrique, de sensibilité et de détectivité ; en particulier, le poly(pyrrole):PSS (PPY:PSS) a été synthétisé et introduit comme couche de transport de trous (HTL) en remplacement du PEDOT:PSS, améliorant la stabilité environnementale. Les phototransistors organiques (OPT) ont été étudiés de façon comparative dans des architectures monocomposant et à hétérojonction en volume (BHJ) afin d'élucider les corrélations entre transport de charge et réponse électro-optique. En se concentrant sur les systèmes PM6\:Y6, l'analyse quantitative de la réponse photoélectrique et de la vitesse de commutation démontre la faisabilité de phototransistors à haute sensibilité et faible consommation, et précise comment le rapport donneur\:accepteur et l'ingénierie interfaciale gouvernent les performances photoélectriques. Un inverseur logique basé sur BHJ a en outre été réalisé pour valider les caractéristiques de fonctionnement et la stabilité de commande au niveau circuit. Enfin, une peau électronique (e-skin) auto-alimentée à base de TENG, dotée de capacités d'auto-cicatrisation, a permis l'acquisition fiable de biosignaux tels que l'EMG et l'ECG, tandis qu'une analyse assistée par apprentissage automatique a rendu possible la classification des types de mouvement et des applications de rétroaction. Dans l'ensemble, en reliant de manière cohérente l'auto-alimentation, l'amélioration des performances, l'intégration aux circuits et l'interface avec le vivant, ce travail fournit des fondations technologiques de niveau plateforme pour les futures applications en santé connectée, biosenseurs intelligents et circuits neuromorphiques.

title: Iodinated Heptamethinecyanine Dye / Dextran-Polyacrylamide Polymer / Gold Nanorods Nanohybrid with Plasmon Enhanced NIR Optical Response for Potential Bioimaging and Biosensing Applications
authors: Oleg Yeshchenko; Oles Fedotov; Pavlo Khort; Dmytro Kobzev; Anatoliy Tatarets; Mykola Ischenko; Volodymyr Doroschuk; Pavlo Virych; Natalia Kutsevol
abstract: Abstract Multifunctional hybrid nanoplatforms operating within the near-infrared (NIR) biological transparency window hold immense potential for various biomedical applications. In this work, we report the synthesis and optical investigation of water-soluble 3-component nanohybrids based on iodinated heptamethine cyanine dyes (2I-HITC and 4I-HITC), a star-like dextran-graft-polyacrylamide copolymer matrix (D6-PAA), and plasmonic gold nanorods (AuNRs) with longitudinal surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) at 660 nm (AuNR660) and 745 nm (AuNR745). The D6-PAA polymer matrix effectively reduces hydrophobic dye aggregation as well as encapsulates dye molecules and AuNRs. Spectral tuning of the LSPR of AuNRs to match the NIR absorption and emission bands of the dyes led to strong plasmon-enhanced photoluminescence (SEPL) and Raman scattering (SERS). The optical response exhibited a non-monotonic concentration dependence dictated by the competition between plasmonic enhancement and non-radiative Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) quenching. Due to weaker FRET quenching and stronger local electromagnetic field hot spots, the 2I-HITC/D6-PAA/AuNR745 nanohybrid achieved the highest enhancement factors for both PL (26.8-fold) and SERS (25.4-fold under 785 nm excitation). Theoretical calculations using Boyd’s local-field enhancement model strongly corroborated the experimental SERS results, confirming the spatial proximity of the functional components within the polymer matrix. These findings highlight the three-component 2I-HITC/D6-PAA/AuNR745 nanohybrid as a potential platform for high-sensitivity NIR fluorescence bioimaging and diagnostic SERS sensing.

title: Adhesive-Free Paper-Derived Laser-Induced Graphene-Hydrogel Interfaces for Label-Free Bacterial Sensing
authors: Fatemeh Hassanpour; Kimia Noroozi; Farshid Noormohammadi; Michael J. Forrester; Peter Meyer; Kaylee B. Herrig; Bryce Chun; Nicole N. Hashemi; Eric W. Cochran; Laura Jarboe; Patrick A. Johnson; Reza Montazami
abstract: Abstract Wearable and disposable bioelectronic sensors require conductive materials that combine electrochemical performance with mechanical compliance, biocompatibility, and environmental sustainability. Yet, most bioelectronics, including those fabricated using laser-induced graphene (LIG) platforms, still rely almost exclusively on non-degradable polyimide substrates, or on transfer methods that require adhesives, solvents, or cryogenic processing. Here, we report a sustainable biosensing platform in which patterned LIG is generated on uncoated paperboard and transferred onto a glyceraldehyde-cross-linked gelatin-glycerol hydrogel by simple contact under ambient conditions, without adhesives or intermediate solvents. The porous LIG forms a continuous, gap-free interface with the hydrogel and retains its graphitic structure after transfer and nine months of ambient storage. The resulting LIG-hydrogel composite is mechanically compliant and electrochemically active, exhibiting reversible mechano-ionic and strain-dependent piezoresistive responses. Configured as a two-electrode, non-Faradaic impedance biosensor with an integrated agar reservoir, the platform discriminates Escherichia coli-containing from sterile samples within 2–3 h through bacteria-associated changes in medium impedance, with the control-bacteria separation maximized near 25 kHz (p = 0.009). This adhesive-free, ambient-processed platform offers a scalable route to environmentally sustainable, disposable, and label-free biosensors.

title: Stretchable Sensors For E-skin Patches
authors: Ayşenur Acuner; Cem Bayram; Dincer Gokcen; Gokcen Birlik Demirel
abstract: Electronic skin (e-skin) is an important wearable technology designed to mimic the properties of human skin, which has significant potential for the development of personalized healthcare. Flexibility, biocompatibility, and conformability to skin surfaces are important properties of e-skin materials that provide multifunctional sensing capabilities. These systems can provide continuous, non-invasive real-time monitoring of various physical and chemical health indicators while enabling long-term data collection. Advances in materials science play a significant role in the development of e-skin technologies. This chapter discusses the fundamental material requirements for e-skin applications such as biocompatibility, mechanical performance, and sensing functionality. It highlights critical factors in material selection and design, as well as representative examples of sensor operating mechanisms. It also examines the major challenges facing current e-skin systems, including issues related to long-term wearability, signal stability, and data integration, while exploring emerging strategies to overcome these limitations. In this context, ongoing research and innovation in e-skin technology is expected to drive the next generation of wearable health monitoring systems that offer transformative potential for personalized healthcare, disease prevention, and human–machine interfaces.

title: Highly Spiro‐Configured Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Materials for Improving Electroluminescence Efficiencies and Reducing Roll‐Offs of OLEDs
authors: Xia Lan; Ruiqi Sun; Chengxi Lin; Zujin Zhao
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials continue to encounter a significant challenge in concurrently attaining high solid‐state photoluminescence efficiency and minimal singlet–triplet energy splitting (Δ E ST ). In this study, a rigid and sterically hindered weak electron acceptor (SAO) is constructed by incorporating a spiro structure into a carbonyl‐based fused‐ring acceptor. Subsequent combination with two weak electron donors, spiro[acridine‐9,9'‐xanthene] and spiro[acridine‐9,9'‐fluorene], yields two sky‐blue TADF emitters (SAO‐X and SAO‐F). The enhanced molecular rigidity conferred by this design improves thermal stability and boosts photoluminescence quantum yields to nearly unity. They exhibit small Δ E ST values (24‒38 meV), rapid reverse intersystem crossing rates of (1.9‒2.7 × 10 6 s −1 ), and short delayed fluorescence lifetimes (1.2‒2.0 µs) in film states. Furthermore, the non‐doped organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) fabricated using SAO‐X and SAO‐F as emitters display bright sky‐blue emission with a maximum external quantum efficiency ( η ext,max ) of 22.8% and a low efficiency roll‐off of 3.9%. Moreover, the doped OLEDs achieve a record‐high η ext,max of 44.1%. Notably, SAO‐X and SAO‐F can also serve as effective sensitizers for the multiresonance TADF emitter tCzphB‐Fl in hyperfluorescence OLEDs, providing impressive η ext,max s of 40.3% and 39.4%. These results demonstrate that these highly spiro‐configured TADF emitters are promising candidates for OLEDs.
